The Citizens have always maintained their innocence and had until Friday, October 2 to appeal the verdict. items.text: San Francisco's car crime has plunged. How much credit does Flock deserve?
items.article: San Francisco leaders say AI-powered cameras helped drive a dramatic decline in car crime. We examine the evidence — and whether the city can keep its high-tech dragnet without sacrificing civil liberties. SAN FRANCISCO - JUNE 13: An automated license plate reader is seen mounted on a pole on June 13, 2024, in San Francisco. Justin Sullivan/Getty Images/Getty Images North America hide caption This article first appeared in the Planet Money newsletter. You can sign up here . In August 2022, my truck was stolen on the streets of San Francisco. I had only lived in the city for a year, but it was the third time it was stolen or broken into. This led me to report on the epidemic of car crime around the city and how anti-theft technology made some cars harder to steal than others. The Bay Area then had one of the highest rates of car theft in the nation. Four years later, something remarkable has happened: car thefts in SF are down almost 59%, and car break-ins are down more than 82%, according to our analysis of SFPD crime data comparing January through August of 2026 with the same months in 2022. And once again, technology is a prominent part of the story. San Francisco's law enforcement leaders tell us that greater use of surveillance technology — including a controversial, AI-powered license plate camera system made by Flock Safety — has been crucial to this drop in car crime. items.text: More bad news for California's imperiled Joshua trees
items.article: The Trump administration canceled Joshua Tree National Park's plans to address its fire-prone future. Last October, a hiker who lit toilet paper on fire in Joshua Tree National Park reportedly started a fire near popular Black Rock Campground, forcing an evacuation of the campground and the closure of a visitor center and nearby trails. The fire started nearly two weeks into a government shutdown that left national parks with minimal staffing. The Black Rock Fire burned 72 acres. Earlier that same year, the Eureka Fire scorched over 200 acres in the Covington Flats area of the park, a higher-elevation region that’s considered crucial “climate refugia” habitat , where the threatened western Joshua tree stands a better chance of surviving as climate change brings hotter and drier conditions. And in 2023, the Geology Fire burned over 1,000 acres, killing an estimated 3,000 Joshua trees in a backcountry area of the park. Historically, fires that started in this part of the Mojave Desert have burned out quickly, as the sparse landscape made it difficult for fires to spread from one desert plant to another. But in recent decades, a combination of invasive grasses and hotter, drier conditions have brought Joshua Tree National Park into a new era of wildfire. Despite those new threats, the Trump administration recently canceled more than $1 million in projects that would have helped the park restore burned areas and prepare for future fires. items.text: Girlfriends should be even more worried about GTA 6 as official age rating confirms new details
items.article: It's the most hotly anticipated game release of the year Rockstar have confirmed the age rating of the upcoming GTA 6 , after some women expressed concern about the game's content. The new Grand Theft Auto game is one of the most hotly-anticipated games of the year, and is the first main game released in the franchise since 2013's Grand Theft Auto V . And it wouldn't be a Grand Theft Auto game release without controversy about the game's content, with the series even previously being accused of glamorising crime . This time however it's not so much the criminal underworld and violent aspects which have seen people worried, but some women taking to social media to voice concern about the game involving an optional relationship storyline. Now, the game's age rating has been confirmed, and like many other games in the franchise it has been rated as 18. But it's one particular part of why exactly the game was given that rating which may cause further consternation among people worried about their partners developing some sort of artificial relationship with the characters.

items.text: The forgotten slimming pill that could be better for you than Mounjaro... and it's cheaper: Our experts reveal everything you need to know about the drug - and how it's particularly good for people who binge-eat or have cravings
items.article: Weight-loss jabs and pills such as Wegovy and Mounjaro have the glamour of association with celebrity users, including Oprah Winfrey. Published: 01:00, 29 September 2026 | Updated: 02:14, 29 September 2026 Weight-loss jabs and pills such as Wegovy and Mounjaro have the glamour of association with celebrity users, including Oprah Winfrey . The public has embraced them too, with millions of people taking the medicines in the UK. But amid the enthusiasm for those medications, known as GLP-1s, an older, cheaper anti-obesity drug that might be a better choice for some patients is being ‘overlooked’, a leading expert says. Mysimba, a pill containing naltrexone and bupropion, is licensed in the UK as a treatment for people with obesity, or who are overweight with weight-related health problems. Available only via private clinics, it is cheaper than GLP-1s. In trials, people using Mysimba lost around 8 per cent of their starting weight. That is lower than the amount lost by people using the latest GLP-1s. In studies of Mounjaro, participants taking the highest doses lost around 22 per cent of their body weight.

items.article: A big options bet involving the utility sector could indicate a top in yields. As the U.S. bond market firmed Thursday and the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) posted its best intraday rally in at least a month, some less notable but equally important action for bond bulls happened in two corners of the options market. In equities, about an hour after the opening bell on Thursday, a string of options bets in the State Street Utilities Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLU) sent options volume in the fund to 10 times the 30-day average, according to CBOE LiveVol data and SpotGamma. It centered around a $1 million trade betting that the group stops going down or even rallies. As bonds have fallen — driving rates higher — utility stocks have been hard hit as the dividend-rich sector faces increased competition for its payouts from fixed income. Specifically, that trader sold 5,000 of the 39-strike puts expiring in mid-January for $695,000, and an equal amount of the 42-strike calls expiring the same day for $400,000. With XLU trading just above $39 at the time of the trade, it's a bet with a maximum payout between $39 and $42 by expiry. While the trade is not an aggressive bet on a rally in utilities, it a sign that some traders believe the sector is done falling and that rates may have topped out. items.text: To sync or swim? Learning how to gracefully agree to disagree
items.article: Real partnership doesn’t need two people to share the same passions, views or lifestyle. It’s enough to leave each other room to evolve in different directions. Is it possible to live and let live when you are committed to building a life together? In a culture that promotes being “one entity” as a couple, can one even allow oneself to follow a different growth path, which is not similar to your partner’s? Post pandemic, Bengaluru-based lawyer Dina (37), a client of mine has been on a path to downsizing her life. Ved (37), her entrepreneur husband, has seen his venture flourish since then. He wants to flaunt his success by supersizing acquisitions, making grand social gestures and maximising their lifestyle. For Dina and Ved, the minimalist and maximalist attitude is indeed a drastic juxtaposition. For any reasonably successful relationship, being aligned on the kind of lifestyle to lead together is among the most important vectors. Money management and parenting style being the other important ones. The last couple of years have been particularly hard as Dina is getting more confident about the minimalistic path and Ved more grand in the lifestyle he is drawn to. Her arguments are heard and perhaps even understood by Ved but he is not in a place to follow Dina’s lead. items.text: Why your Habs tickets cost more than any other NHL team's this season
items.article: Montreal Canadiens fans wanting to see their team play at home this season will have to pay a premium for tickets, with average prices at the Bell Centre higher than anywhere else across the NHL. Following a successful year that saw the Montreal Canadiens reach the Eastern Conference final, tickets to see the Habs play at home this season will be the most expensive in the NHL — a new feat for the historic franchise. According to sports betting and online casino research firm Bookies.com and TicketData.com, a website devoted to tracking resale ticket prices, Canadiens fans will pay an average of over $220 for cheapest tickets — more than double the league average — to see their team in action this season. Montreal is one of the biggest markets in the NHL, and the Canadiens consistently rank in the top five among priciest tickets in the league, with the Toronto Maple Leafs leading the pack most seasons over the past decade. Moshe Lander, a sports economist and associate professor at Concordia University, says although Habs fans might not be happy about the high ticket costs, they shouldn’t be surprised. “Unfortunately for Montreal Canadiens fans, a little bit of success is the type of thing that reawakens a lot of dormant fans.” 3 things fans should know about the Montreal Canadiens this NHL season

items.text: New Pokémon merch is literally out of this world
items.article: Now is the best time to celebrate World Space Week and your love for all things Pokémon with a new, exciting collaboration. No need to blast off again to purchase these amazing items, though We've always said Pokémon needs a game set entirely in space so we can see all our favorite characters in a space suit. While that dream hasn't been realized yet, the Pokémon Company has taken another step toward making it happen: space Pokémon merchandise. In celebration of World Space Week — which takes place from Oct. 4 to Oct. 10 — The Pokémon Company International and the European Space Agency (ESA) have teamed up to take everyone's favorite electric-type Pokémon to the stars in an effort to "inspire the next generation of explorers." The exclusive collection is now officially available for purchase. This new collaboration brings a range of items, including exclusive space-themed selections, with some available only on the Pokémon Center's US website. When we say some of this new merchandise is the most adorable thing we've ever seen, that's putting it mildly. Pokémon's mascot steals the show with two new Pikachu plushies in astronaut gear. The male variant is white, while the female is a crisp dark blue. The collection also includes pins and patches featuring Pikachu in its space suit, along with other Pokémon like Lunatone, Minior, and Cosmog — none of which would look out of place floating in the cosmos.

items.text: Does Google’s new model really catch up to OpenAI, Anthropic at the frontier?
items.article: Google has been trailing OpenAI and Anthropic for much of 2026, analysts say Gemini 4 puts it back in the frontier AI conversation. This report is from this week's The Tech Download newsletter. Like what you see? You can subscribe here. 2026 has been a turbulent year for Google's AI hopes and dreams. Things started well. Gemini 3, which launched towards the end of 2025, put Google very much in the frontier AI conversation. But for much of the rest of this year, it's Anthropic and OpenAI that have been at the forefront of AI advances. Google will undoubtedly be hoping the release of a new flagship model, Gemini 4 Argon, changes that. When Demis Hassabis stepped down as CEO of DeepMind, Google's AI lab, in August, I wrote that new boss Koray Kavukcuoglu was inheriting a race to catch-up with Sam Altman and Dario Amodei's companies.

items.key: ai:i traveled abroad for 2 weeks with only a carry-on and a personal item. here's what worked — and what i wish i'd left behind.
items.text: I traveled abroad for 2 weeks with only a carry-on and a personal item. Here's what worked — and what I wish I'd left behind.
items.article: While traveling abroad for two weeks, I was so glad I packed a worldwide adapter and wired headphones. There are other items I wish I'd left at home. When I set out on my first solo international trip — a two-week journey through Ireland, the UK, and Iceland, along with pit stops in New York and Chicago — I was plagued by one question: What should I pack? Since I was only bringing a carry-on suitcase and a backpack, every item had to earn its place. By the time I got home, I made plenty of memories — and came to a much clearer sense of what I'd pack again, and what I'd leave behind. Here are four items I was glad I brought, and three I could've gone without. Even though I went on this trip in the summer, I knew several places I was visiting would be rainy. But because of the different climates I was going to, I quibbled over how warm I wanted a jacket to be. I settled on an older, rain-resistant jacket that had lost some of its fluff rather than a light windbreaker. The jacket kept me warm in the Icelandic mist and didn't overwhelm me in New York during evening showers. Right before my trip, I decided to get Icelandic krónur, British pounds, and some euros.

items.key: ai:he escaped as his partners fell. how hunt for terrorist hashim moosa ended
items.text: He escaped as his partners fell. How hunt for terrorist Hashim Moosa ended
items.article: This week, LeT commander Mohammad Asif was killed in a gunfight in Yusmarg. Security agencies say the group operated across the Pir Panjal for nearly five years, carrying out attacks in Rajouri, Gulmarg and Pahalgam before its members were gradually tracked down. For nearly five years, Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) commander Mohammad Asif moved through the forests of the Pir Panjal and Kashmir Valley, part of a network behind a string of deadly attacks targeting civilians and security forces while evading capture. On Wednesday, Asif, also known as Hashim Moosa, was killed in a gunfight with security forces — the latest breakthrough in the hunt for the network, which was linked to attacks across the region, including the April 2025 Pahalgam attack that killed 26 people , including a local pony operator. According to officials, LeT commander Mohammad Asif, whom sources describe as highly trained and battle-hardened, had been acting alone after his associate Yasir was killed in a gunfight in Ashdar Gali in the upper reaches of Dodapathri tourist resort last month. Sources say Asif – as well as his two partners Yasir and Sulaiman – infiltrated the forests of Jammu in late 2021 and have been active since, with investigators saying they were responsible for several deadly terror attacks on the Rajouri-Poonch axis. Officials claim that it was this group that was involved in several gunfights in Bhatta Durian in Rajouri in October 2021, leading to the killings of as many as nine soldiers.

items.key: ai:how claims of 'masking' in adhd are impacting diagnosis
items.text: How claims of 'masking' in ADHD are impacting diagnosis
items.article: The idea that people can 'mask' symptoms of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder has contributed to the rise in diagnoses, but is it based on good evidence? ADHD is a medical condition that is currently under intense scrutiny. Numbers of those diagnosed are rising, waiting lists are lengthening – and the benefits bill is swelling. Along with similar rises in autism and mental ill health , the trend is causing such concern, it’s the subject of a government investigation, due to report shortly . One aspect of the rise in ADHD that gets less attention is “masking” – the idea that people cover up symptoms such as disorganisation, fidgeting and daydreaming to cope better with school or work. This may have contributed to a significant portion of the rise in ADHD diagnoses over the past decade, and possibly to the rise in autism too, say experts. But some doctors and researchers are sceptical about the entire premise of masking. “It’s an unfalsifiable concept,” said Professor Uta Frith, an Emeritus Professor of Cognitive Development at University College London. The government review into ADHD, autism and mental health conditions was ordered by Health Secretary Wes Streeting last year.
